idiom_name: Node worker_threads MessageChannel/MessagePort or BullMQ Worker on a Redis queue
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no blocking receive, so the channel is either an event-loop queue with exactly one consumer loop or a MessagePort pair: the worker_threads MessageChannel delivers each posted message to the port's listener exactly once, which is the in-process realization. Distributed Node code uses a broker queue, and BullMQ - built on Redis, with exactly-once queue semantics as its stated goal and at-least-once as the worst case - is the dominant library; a Worker claims each job once, and adding workers is the Competing Consumers scaling step.
pitfalls: An EventEmitter is not a channel: every listener sees every event, so using one where exactly one consumer must handle each message silently duplicates work.
Messages posted to a MessagePort queue up invisibly until a listener (or start()) begins consuming; there is no backpressure warning, only growth.
An in-memory array/queue with no bound grows until the process runs out of memory - Node has no blocking producer to stop.
